clue.text: Took a dip, evenly spread, having too much on one's plate

definitions.text: having too much on one's plate

parts.note: to take a dip is to go for a swim, so in the past tense it is swam

indicators.note: evenly means taking the even-numbered letters, the second, fourth and sixth, of spread

explanation.surface: Someone who went for a swim and then faced a lavish buffet spread, overwhelmed by the food piled up.
explanation.walkthrough: The plate and the spread suggest food, but 'having too much on one's plate' is the idiom for being overloaded with work.
explanation.definitionFit: To be swamped is to be overwhelmed with tasks, the same idea as the idiom of an overfull plate.

clue.text: Be critical of the woman cuddling pet

indicators.note: cuddling means the word for the woman wraps around the pet

parts.note: she is the pronoun for the woman
a cat is a typical household pet

explanation.surface: Disapproving of a woman who is always hugging her pet.
explanation.definitionFit: To scathe is to attack with withering criticism, the root of scathing.

clue.text: Rules for Xmas crackers interrupted by vino, regularly

indicators.note: interrupted by means the picked letters are put inside the scrambled word
crackers means mad, so the letters of Xmas are scrambled
regularly means taking every other letter of vino, here the second and fourth

explanation.surface: Christmas cracker etiquette, with wine breaking in now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crackers' suggests Christmas crackers but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Axioms are self-evident principles or maxims, accepted rules of thought.

clue.text: Cite former vice president's outside choice

indicators.note: outside means the vice president's name sits around the word for cite

parts.note: Mike Pence was US vice president from 2017 to 2021
to cite is to refer to

explanation.surface: Quoting a past vice president's choice made outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A preference is the option one favours, a choice made over others.

clue.text: Where the pearl diver starts working

definitions.text: Where the pearl diver starts working

indicators.note: working means the letters are put to work in a new order
starts means the first letters of pearl and diver are taken

explanation.surface: A pearl diver begins the job down in the deep sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: THE plus P and D, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Pearl divers work far below the surface, down in the deep water where oysters lie.

clue.text: Delicacy could make one fretful

indicators.note: could make says the letters of fretful can be rearranged to form another word

explanation.surface: An expensive treat might leave someone anxious, perhaps about the price or about eating it properly.
explanation.definitionFit: A truffle, the prized underground fungus or the chocolate sweet, is a classic gourmet delicacy.

clue.text: Underscore young people, being eager, sent flying

indicators.note: sent flying means scattered, so the letters of eager and sent are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Keen youngsters being ejected from somewhere in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underscore' looks like underlining, but read as under score it means under twenty, a score being twenty.
explanation.definitionFit: Teenagers are youths aged thirteen to nineteen, all below a score of years.

clue.text: Philanthropist abandons half the Hebridean islands

indicators.note: abandons half means the front half of the word for a philanthropist is dropped and the back half kept

parts.note: an altruist acts selflessly for others, like a philanthropist

explanation.surface: A charitable donor deserting half of a Scottish archipelago.
explanation.walkthrough: Uist covers North Uist and South Uist, linked islands of the Outer Hebrides off Scotland, so the plural definition is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: North and South Uist form a pair of linked islands in Scotland's Outer Hebrides.

clue.text: Obvious jingoistic tirade?

parts.note: jingoism is flag-waving patriotism
a rant is a tirade

explanation.surface: A patriotic rant that leaves no doubt about the speaker's views.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the wordplay is a quirky reading: a flag rant would be a jingoistic tirade.
explanation.definitionFit: Flagrant means glaring and conspicuous, especially of wrongdoing that is plain to see.

clue.text: Nearly seven pillar boxes then appeared in London

definitions.text: pillar boxes then appeared in London
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the year 1855, when the first pillar boxes were installed in London

explanation.walkthrough: A pillar box is a free-standing red British postbox; London's first appeared in 1855. Read as a time, the same figures are 18:55.
explanation.definitionFit: The figures 1855 serve both as a clock time just short of seven and as the year of the first London postboxes.

clue.text: Live bear

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to dwell or reside somewhere
second meaning: to tolerate or put up with

explanation.walkthrough: 'Live bear' reads as a wild animal, but the two words are separate verbs with the same five-letter synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to dwell somewhere (abide in a place) and to tolerate something (cannot abide it).

clue.text: Media silence about northern recruiters

parts.note: the press is the news media

indicators.note: about means the word for silence goes around the letter for northern

parts.note: to gag someone is to silence them; a gag is the thing that silences

explanation.surface: Journalists hushing up a story about the north of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: A press gang was a band that forced men into naval service; British ships used them in the 18th century.
explanation.definitionFit: A press gang conscripted sailors by force, so its members were recruiters of a brutal kind.

clue.text: Shark H?

parts.note: H is the head, or first letter, of the word hammer

explanation.surface: A one-letter riddle presented as if a shark could be labelled by a single letter.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: the head of HAMMER is its first letter, H, which is exactly what the clue shows.
explanation.definitionFit: The hammerhead is a species of shark with a broad, flattened, hammer-shaped head.

clue.text: Last killer leaving America dry

indicators.note: leaving means the letters for America are taken away from the killer's name

parts.note: in Shakespeare's Julius Caesar, Brutus delivers the final stab to Caesar ('Et tu, Brute?')
US is the United States, America

explanation.surface: The final murderer departs the United States, leaving the place parched.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare, Caesar is stabbed last by Brutus, his friend. Remove US to leave the wine term.
explanation.definitionFit: Brut is the label for the driest style of champagne and sparkling wine.

clue.text: Weapon that's not targeted is empty threat — some work you reported in survey

indicators.note: in means the following pieces go inside the word for survey

parts.note: to scan is to survey

indicators.note: empty means only the outer letters of threat are kept

parts.note: its first and last letters
an erg is a unit, or amount, of work in physics

indicators.note: reported means the word you is heard and written as the letter that sounds like it

parts.note: you sounds like the letter U

explanation.surface: A survey reporting that an empty threat is a matter of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some work' is ERG, the physics unit of work.
explanation.definitionFit: A scattergun fires a spray of shot, so it hits widely rather than aiming at one precise point.

clue.text: Transience of intrinsic nature said to follow Welshman

indicators.note: to follow means the homophone comes after the Welshman's name

parts.note: Evan is a typical Welsh man's name

indicators.note: said means the word for intrinsic nature is heard, then written as it sounds

parts.note: essence is the intrinsic nature of a thing

explanation.surface: A philosopher musing on the fleeting essence of things, as voiced after a Welshman.
explanation.definitionFit: Evanescence is the quality of fading away quickly, which is what transience describes.

clue.text: An item of underwear sold in outrageous new style initially causes injuries

parts.note: an gives the letter A
a bra is an item of women's underwear

indicators.note: initially means taking the first letter of each of the next five words

explanation.surface: A bra sold in a daring new design causes chafing and harm.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrasions are scrapes where the skin is rubbed away, a common type of minor wound.

clue.text: Understanding medicine is primarily needed in hepatic transplant

indicators.note: transplant means the letters are moved around into a new arrangement
primarily means the first letter of medicine

explanation.surface: Medicine is essential in a liver transplant operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hepatic' means of the liver, which makes 'transplant' look surgical, but it is the signal to rearrange M with HEPATIC.
explanation.definitionFit: An empathic person shares and grasps others' feelings, showing compassionate understanding.

clue.text: Hairy sport supporting international organisation

indicators.note: supporting in a down answer means this piece sits below the one for the international organisation

parts.note: UN is the United Nations, an international organisation
read as S plus port; a haven is a port, so port becomes haven after the S

explanation.surface: A burly sportsman backing a global body such as the UN.
explanation.walkthrough: The same trick as in GRAVE: split sport into S and port, then swap port for its synonym haven. In a down clue, 'supporting' puts it below UN.
explanation.definitionFit: An unshaven face still has stubble or whiskers on it, so it looks bristly.

clue.text: Digital products without party broadcast documentaries

indicators.note: broadcast means the remaining letters are scattered and rearranged
without means the party word is removed from documentaries

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: Television documentaries shown without any political party broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digital products' sounds like electronics, but digital here means to do with fingers. Taking DO from documentaries leaves CUMENTARIES to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A manicure set holds the tools for grooming fingernails, so its contents are products for the digits.

clue.text: End of life, an evolution

indicators.note: an evolution is a change of form, so the letters of life and an develop into a new order

explanation.surface: Musing on death, the conclusion of life, as a stage of evolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of life' looks like the definition, but only 'End' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A finale is the closing part of a show or piece of music, its conclusion.

clue.text: DJ's part in city rave ultimately secured by playing LPs

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles

indicators.note: secured by means the letter is held inside the jumbled letters
playing means the letters of LPs are rearranged
ultimately means the last letter of rave

explanation.surface: A disc jockey playing records at a city rave.
explanation.walkthrough: DJ looks like a disc jockey, but it is a dinner jacket, the British name for a tuxedo.
explanation.definitionFit: Lapels are the folded front flaps of a jacket's collar, part of a dinner jacket.

clue.text: Some schoolteacher's suffering

indicators.note: some means only part of the next word is used, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: Part of a teacher's lot is pain and hardship.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache is a continuous dull pain, one kind of suffering.

clue.text: As a diet of bananas, with a spice

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters go wild and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe for living on nothing but bananas, plus a pinch of spice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' looks like part of the diet, but it is slang for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Asafoetida is a pungent resin-based seasoning used widely in Indian cooking.

clue.text: See 8
See 8
Make love in retreat, mostly with one aristocrat

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the word for retreat is dropped

parts.note: a haven is a place of retreat or refuge
I is the Roman numeral for one
toff is British slang for an upper-class person

explanation.surface: An amorous tryst at a hideaway with a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: To have it off is British slang for having sex.
explanation.definitionFit: The British slang phrase is a crude idiom for having sex.

clue.text: Serious grant?

parts.note: read as G plus rant; a rave is a rant, so G with RAVE gives the clue word

explanation.surface: A solemn award of money, or a stern man named Grant.
explanation.walkthrough: A favourite trick of this setter: split grant into G and rant, then swap rant for its synonym rave.
explanation.definitionFit: Grave means solemn and weighty, a straightforward synonym for serious.

clue.text: Nose and ears not a game

parts.note: conk is British slang for the nose

indicators.note: not means the letter a is left out of ears

explanation.surface: A face is just nose and ears, and nothing to play with.
explanation.walkthrough: Conkers is a British children's game played with horse chestnuts on strings, each player trying to smash the other's.
explanation.definitionFit: Conkers is a traditional playground pastime with chestnuts threaded on strings.

clue.text: Americans awfully keen to invade backward state

indicators.note: to invade means the rearranged letters go inside the word for state
backward means the word for state is read from the end

parts.note: to state is to say

indicators.note: awfully signals that the letters of keen are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: Eager Americans storming a state that is behind the times.
explanation.definitionFit: Yankees is a common nickname for people from the United States.
